Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:65: And therefore it is fitting for a person to resemble his Creator, as they said (Berachot 58b, Tikkunei Zohar, page 1b), it suffices for the servant to be like his master - and just as, in exile, our Father is grieved in our own grief, as it is said (Isaiah 63:9), "in all their affliction, He was afflicted" - and it is explained, "not a messenger" [reading lo without vav], "but He Himself" was afflicted, so that the trouble reached even the supernal One, as explained in the Bahir and likewise in the Zohar, Parashat Vayera (page 120b) - so it is fitting for a person to be afflicted [in solidarity].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:66: And just as He weeps, as it is written (Jeremiah 13:17), "my soul shall weep in secret places because of pride," and it is explained in Tractate Chagigah (5b), the Holy One, blessed be He, has a place where He weeps, and its name is "secret places" - so it is fitting that he too weep.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:67: And just as, from the day the Temple was destroyed, there is no laughter before Him, as we learn in the first chapter of Avodah Zarah (3b): Rav Acha of Migdal said to Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak, since the Temple was destroyed there is no laughter before the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Isaiah 42:14), "I have been silent from of old" - so it is not fitting that his mouth be filled with laughter, along the lines of Reish Lakish (Berachot 31a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:68: And so, when he thinks that through our sins, voice was separated from speech, for in exile she says, "I was mute, silent" (Psalms 39:3) - so it is fitting that he endure and be silent when they disgrace him or provoke him to anger - for the Holy One, blessed be He, endures foreigners dancing in His own Sanctuary because of us, and His great Name is profaned through us, so how should a person not endure anger or disgrace from his fellow, and the like, and especially from a Gentile, as it is written (Lamentations 3:30), "let him give his cheek to the one who strikes him; let him be filled with disgrace; for the LORD does not cast off forever," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:69: And just as, through our sins, He causes the lowliness of the Shechinah, as it says (Isaiah 26:5), "He shall bring it low, He shall bring it low," and so on, "to the dust," as explained in the Gate of Fear (chapter 9) and the Gate of Repentance (chapter 7) - so it is fitting that he be lowly, and not choose lofty places. And just as her voice is low, as it is written (Isaiah 29:4), "and you shall speak low from the ground, and your speech shall whisper from the dust" - so it is fitting that his voice be lowered like a mourner, and this is (Psalms 35:14), "like a mourner for a mother, I bowed down mourning." And he should not adorn himself with fine clothing except on the Sabbath and festivals, when she takes off the weekday garments of exile and puts on royal garments, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 3b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:70: And so it is fitting not to indulge in the pleasures of the world on weekdays, but rather to restrict himself as much as possible - for on weekdays the world is clothed in the lower husk, which is "another god," and it follows that he indulges before other gods. And they explained this matter in the Zohar, Parashat Vayakhel (page 207b), concerning one who fasts on the Sabbath, saying that his remedy is to fast one day during the week, a fast for the fast - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said, what is the reason? Because he nullified the Sabbath's delight, he must nullify the weekday's delight - and if he nullifies the Sabbath's delight and indulges during the week, he is like one who considers another god more than he considers the Holy One, blessed be He - the supernal holy spirit of holiness that rested upon him was not indulged and he nullified it from himself, [while] another, weekday spirit that afterward rests upon the world he considers important and indulges - then they return and exact punishment from him in this world and in the World to Come, and therefore another fast is needed on the first weekday, at the time that weekday spirit rests upon the world - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:71: And so, for the reason of the Shechinah's exile, it is fitting to be afflicted in one's food and not indulge, since she, in exile, has no clothing or conjugal right, as is known (Tikkunei Zohar, page 22a-b). And so it is fitting to go from place to place, to be exiled along with the exile of the Shechinah, just as she is exiled from place to place, as explained at the beginning of the Introduction to the Tikkunim (page 1b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:72: And concerning the merit of one who is afflicted for the sake of the Shechinah, it is said (Psalms 146:5), "happy is he whose help is the God of Jacob, whose hope [shivro] is in the LORD his God," as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel, page 198a) - these are its words: "shivro" [his hope], not "his hope" [tikvato] nor "his trust" [bitchono], but "shivro" - do not read "shivro" [his hope] but "shivro" [his brokenness/breaking] - for it pleases the righteous to break themselves, breaking upon breaking, and all for the LORD his God, along the lines of (Psalms 44:23), "for Your sake we are killed all day long," (ibid. 69:8), "for Your sake I have borne reproach" - along the lines of Jacob, of whom it is written (Genesis 42:1), "and Jacob saw that there was grain [shever] in Egypt" - for he saw the breaking of the exile that he would have in Egypt, and set his strength in the Holy One, blessed be He - and Jacob's sons endured the breaking of the exile and were not changed from the secret of their fathers' faith, and the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, was regularly on their lips in exile - and therefore it is written (Exodus 3:13), "and they shall say to me, what is His name?" - because they knew Him and never forgot Him, and endured the breaking of the exile for the sake of the Holy One, blessed be He - and therefore they merited redemptions, miracles, and many signs. And supernal holy ones, who endure the breaking of the body from place to place for the sake of the Holy One, blessed be He, all the more so - you shall merit that miracles and redemptions be performed for you, and you shall merit the life of the World to Come - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:73: And so King David, peace be upon him, was afflicted over the Shechinah, saying (I Chronicles 17:1), "behold, I dwell in a house of cedars, while the ark of the covenant of the LORD is under curtains," and he said (Psalms 132:4), "if I give sleep to my eyes, or slumber to my eyelids, until I find a place for the LORD." And along these lines, a person should say, when he is at ease in his house: behold, I am in tranquility, ease, and security in my house, while His Shechinah, blessed be He, is cast about in exile because of our sins, and does not even have a tent of curtains - and this is what she says (Song of Songs 1:6), "do not look at me, that I am swarthy, for the sun has gazed upon me; my mother's sons were angry with me, they made me keeper of the vineyards" - as explained in the Zohar (Leviticus, Parashat Tazria, page 45b) concerning the exile of the Shechinah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:74: And therefore even the wealthy person should afflict himself like a poor man in his food and the outlay for his household, and give the rest to charity, as King David, peace be upon him, said (I Chronicles 22:14), "and behold, in my poverty [affliction] I have prepared for the house of the LORD," and so on - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained in the Yerushalmi Pe'ah (chapter 4, halachah 2), "be'onyi" [in my poverty] - "be'inui" [in my self-affliction], for he would fast and dedicate his meal to Heaven. And similarly it is said of many people in Tractate Ta'anit, that they were accustomed to do so.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:75: And if he is himself a poor man, all the more so is it fitting for him to accept suffering with love and not be repulsed by it, and not seek stratagems to become idle from Torah and toil in worldly affairs all day in order to flee from poverty, for poverty was given to him for the atonement of his sins - and if he flees from this, the Creator shall not lack a way to exact his debt from him, and it is not fitting for a servant to flee from beneath his master's sufferings, but rather to accept them with a pleasant countenance. And the merit of the poor exceeds that of the rich, and the proof is David and Solomon - for Solomon was the head of the moon at its fullness, and David at its waning - and David is in the secret of (Psalms 118:22), "the stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone," and ascends to a wondrous level - and so, in the future to come, the cup of blessing shall be given to bless only to David, as explained in Pesachim (119b). And further, concerning the merit of the righteous who are disciplined through poverty and other sufferings, they elaborated at length in Parashat Vayeshev (page 181a), and we copied its words in the Gate of Repentance (chapter 4).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:76: Further, concerning the merit of one who lowers himself for the sake of the Shechinah, it is explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Terumah, page 158b), that he merits a soul from the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah - these are its words: but whoever is poor, who deadens himself for her sake, along your own lines, faithful shepherd, is an offering that descends beneath you - and why? Because whoever lowers himself for the sake of the Shechinah of the Holy One, blessed be He, He descends upon him - and this is what the prophet said (Psalms 138:6), "for the LORD is exalted, yet He regards the lowly, and the haughty," and further (Isaiah 57:15), "for thus says the High and Exalted One who inhabits eternity, and holy is His Name," and so on, "and with the contrite and humble of spirit" - for although I am exalted and holy, I dwell with him who has made himself contrite and humble of spirit for the sake of My Shechinah, to raise her from her lowliness, a crown upon her head - I descend to dwell with him; and after the husband of the Shechinah descends upon a person, she descends from above his head and gives the place of the head to her husband and descends to the King's feet - and the secret of the matter, "the heavens are My throne and the earth My footstool" (Isaiah 66:1) - for from the day a person inherits a soul included from the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, from that hour he is called His son. One teacher said, and is he called His son from that day? From where do we know this? From this verse that David said in the Book of Psalms (Psalms 2:7), "I shall tell of the decree: the LORD said to me, you are My son; this day I have begotten you" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:77: Further, in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 239a): happy is he who strives, in the final exile, to know the Shechinah, to honor her with all commandments, and to endure for her sake several distresses - as it is said, the reward of a bride is distress - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:78: And whoever does not support the Shechinah with his deeds, of him it is said (Isaiah 51:18), "there is none to guide her among all the sons she has borne, and none who takes her by the hand among all the sons she has raised" - and especially he shall receive judgment should the coming of the Messiah occur, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Shemot, page 7b) - these are its words: Rabbi Shimon raised his hands and wept, and said, woe to whoever is present at that time, but happy is the portion of whoever is present and found at that time - woe to whoever is present, because when the Holy One, blessed be He, comes to attend to the doe [i.e., Israel/Shechinah], He shall examine who stands with her, all those found with her, all the deeds of each and every one - and none righteous shall be found, as it is written (Isaiah 63:5), "and I looked, and there was no helper" - and how many afflictions upon afflictions for Israel! Happy is whoever is present and found at that time, for whoever endures in faith shall merit that illumination of the King's joy - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:79: Humility - Ramban wrote of it in a letter he sent to his son, and I have seen fit to copy it, to complete the acquisition of the attribute of humility - these are its words: hear, my son, your father's discipline, and do not forsake it, and always conduct yourself to speak all your words calmly to every person at every time, and through this you shall be saved from anger, which is the bad attribute that causes a person to sin. And so our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Nedarim 22a), whoever becomes angry, all kinds of Gehinnom rule over him, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 11:10), "and remove anger from your heart, and put away evil from your flesh" - and there is no "evil" except Gehinnom, as it is said (Proverbs 16:4), "and even the wicked for the day of evil."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:80: And when you are saved from anger, the attribute of humility, better than all good, shall rise in your heart, as it is said (Proverbs 22:4), "the reward of humility is the fear of the LORD." And through humility, the attribute of fear shall rise in your heart, for you shall always take to heart from where you came and to where you are going, and that you are worm and maggot in your life, all the more so in your death, and before whom you are destined to give judgment and account - before the Glory, as it is said (I Kings 8:27), "behold, the heavens and the heaven of heavens cannot contain You," all the more so the hearts of men - and it says (Jeremiah 23:24), "do I not fill the heavens and the earth, says the LORD?" And when you think of all this, you shall fear your Creator and guard yourself from sin. And through these attributes you shall be joyful with the portion that reaches you. And when you conduct yourself with the attributes of humility, being ashamed before every person, and fearing him and fearing sin, then the spirit of the Shechinah and the radiance of Her glory shall rest upon you, and life, and the life of the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:81: And now, my son, know and see that whoever is proud of heart toward people rebels against the kingdom of Heaven, for he adorns himself in the garment of the Omnipresent, as it is said (Psalms 93:1), "the LORD reigns, He is clothed in pride." And why should a person's heart be proud? If through wealth - "the LORD makes poor and makes rich" (I Samuel 2:7). And if through honor, is it not God's, as it is said (I Chronicles 29:12), "and wealth and honor are from before You" - how shall he boast in the honor of his own Maker? And if he boasts of wisdom, "He removes speech from the trustworthy, and takes away the discernment of the elders" (Job 12:20) - it follows that everything is equal before the Omnipresent, for in His anger He lowers the proud, and in His will He raises the lowly - therefore lower yourself, and the Omnipresent shall raise you up.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:82: Therefore I shall explain how you should conduct yourself with the attribute of humility, to walk in it always. All your words shall be calm, your head bowed, your eyes looking down to the ground and your heart upward, and do not look into the face of a person while speaking with him. Let every person be greater than you in your eyes: if he is wealthy and wise, you must honor him; and if he is poor and you are wealthier than him, or you are wiser than him, think in your heart that you are more guilty than him and he more innocent than you, for if he sins, it is unintentional, while you sin deliberately.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:83: In all your deeds, words, and thoughts, and at all times, think in your heart as though you stand before the Omnipresent and His Shechinah is upon you, for His glory fills the world - and your words shall be with awe and fear, like a servant before his master, and be ashamed before every person - and if a man calls you, do not answer him with a loud voice, but calmly, as one standing before his master.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:84: And be always careful with Torah that you can fulfill, and when you rise from the book, search what you have learned, whether there is something in it that you can fulfill. And examine your deeds morning and evening, and through this all your days shall be in repentance. And remove every extraneous thing from your heart at the time of prayer, and prepare your heart before the Omnipresent, and think about a matter before you utter it from your mouth - and do this all the days of your life, in every single matter, and you shall not sin - and through this all your deeds shall be upright and your prayer clear, pure, clean, focused, and acceptable before the Omnipresent, as it is said (Psalms 10:17), "You shall prepare their heart, You shall incline Your ear."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:85: Read this letter once a week, no less, to fulfill it and walk in it always after the Name, so that you succeed in all your ways, and merit the World to Come, treasured for the righteous - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:86: And when a person strives to fulfill the attribute of humility as Ramban, peace be upon him, wrote in this letter mentioned, there shall follow for him from it the merit of modesty, to be modest in his eating, in the privy, in intimate relations, and in his other ways, and to do all of them for the sake of Heaven, out of his own shame before the Creator, blessed be He, who watches over him always.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:87: And the Ra'avad, peace be upon him, wrote concerning this matter, at the end of the Gate of Holiness, a fine matter I have seen fit to copy his words on - these are its words: and the head of all fences is that a person guard his eyes from everything that is not his own, and even if he diminishes his own gaze even from what is his own - and then he is called modest and shy, along the lines of what they said (Shabbat 53b) of that man whose wife was one-handed, and he never noticed it in his days, and they said of him, how modest is this man, who never noticed his own wife.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:88: And if he guards his eyes, it follows that his heart is guarded, and since his heart and eyes are guarded, it follows that he is entirely guarded - for through three senses in a person, sin is completed, and they are sight, thought, and touch - and if he has the fourth sense, it too serves touch, and this is the sense of hearing, which is not as close to the sense of thought as the sense of sight, for it [sight] immediately brings [an impulse] to the sense of the heart, and the sense of the heart brings it to touch - and of this Scripture warned (Numbers 15:39), "and do not go about [tour] after your heart and after your eyes" - and they said in the Aggadah (Yerushalmi, Berachot, chapter 1, halachah 5), the eye and the heart are the two agents of sin - and so the sage said (Proverbs 23:26), "give me your heart, my son, and let your eyes observe my ways" - give me your heart and your eyes, and I shall know that you are Mine.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:89: And the first of all beginnings is that a person know his Maker and recognize his Creator, and take to heart whom he serves, whom he fears, whose commandments he performs, and who has warned him - as David said to Solomon (I Chronicles 28:9), "my son, know the God of your father, and serve Him with a whole heart" - and although He is hidden from the eyes of every living being, He is nevertheless found in hearts and revealed in thoughts - and let every created being know that he is neither separate from the Creator nor joined to Him, for everything joined [i.e. composite] is bounded, and everything bounded is created anew - and the Creator, blessed be He, has none of these attributes, for He is primordial to everything, neither bounded nor created anew - although the Creator created the created being out of nothing, and if it exists, it exists by His will and desire, to perform His commandments and receive His reward, whether good or bad - for His existence is not hewn out, nor separated, nor bounded, nor diminished, for He is as nothing compared to it [creation], at its beginning and in its likeness [to Him] - and the Creator, blessed be He, is the place of His world, and His world is not His place - and the illustration of the matter: just as the world is full of air, and everything enters within the air and is sensed by it, yet the air is not seen by them. And if Scripture compared man in the Creator's hand to clay in the potter's hand, to let the ear hear what it can grasp, nevertheless the parable is as far from the true likeness as east is from west - for the potter who works the material of clay, although he makes the vessel and precedes the work of the vessel, nevertheless the material from which the vessel is made preceded the craftsman - and therefore the work of the craftsman's hand is hewn before him, and things intervene between him and it, and diminish the sight of his eyes through its own resistance - but the Creator, blessed be He, was preceded by nothing; He created everything out of nothing - and therefore nothing intervenes or separates before Him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:90: And all this the living being shall take to heart, that He sees his Creator, though his own eyes do not see Him - and if the feet and the other organs of the body sin without the heart's intent, behold they are unintentional in the transgression, like a blind man who does not see and eats what comes into his hand under the presumption of permissibility, or spits toward people without knowledge, since he did not know a person was opposite him - it is not fitting to punish him. But whoever sees what he holds in his hand, and if he grasps a forbidden thing and eats it, and if a person stands opposite him and he spits in his face - shall he not be punished with a great punishment for it? So it is with the sin of the heart and thought: since they see their Creator through the power of their own intent and intellect, if they sin against Him and are not ashamed before Him and are not humiliated because of the honor of their Creator standing opposite them, and they harden their faces before their Maker, how great is their punishment - like a person who transgresses the king's command in his very presence, whose punishment is greater and doubled compared to one who is hidden from him and transgresses his command.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:91: And you, son of man, set your heart on all these matters and see their nature, and with your ears hear, and open your eyes, and see the image of your Creator standing before you, and see that He is in heaven and you are on earth, and be guarded from every evil thing - to this point. And along the lines of these words, the author of Sefer HaRokeach wrote at the beginning of his book, in the Root of Holiness - and so as not to be lengthy, we have not copied his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:92: And when the reader remembers what was explained in chapter 1 of the Gate of Fear, concerning fearing this glorious and awesome Name (Deuteronomy 28:58), he shall see with his intellect's eye that from this fear follow modesty, shame, humility, and piety - as it is written in the Zohar (Parashat Naso, page 145a), whoever has fear of Heaven merits humility, and whoever has humility merits piety, and whoever has fear of Heaven merits all of them: humility, as it is written (Proverbs 22:4), "the reward of humility is the fear of the LORD"; piety, as it is written (Psalms 103:17), "but the kindness of the LORD is from everlasting to everlasting upon those who fear Him." We have learned, every person who has piety is called an angel of the LORD of Hosts - to this point, relevant here. And since from fear follow humility and piety, and included in piety are modesty and shame, since he is called an angel of the LORD of Hosts - and it is impossible to acquire these attributes except through a person always placing the supernal providence before him, and thinking that were a person standing over him and watching all his movements, he would fear to do a disgraceful thing out of his own shame before him - so it is fitting that he fear that the Name YHVH stands before him, as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 16:8), "I have set the LORD before me always" - and this is that glorious and awesome Name.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:93: And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Song of Songs section of the Zohar the matter of the Name YHVH being found even below, in this world - these are its words: it is written (Song of Songs 1:4), "draw me after You, let us run" - the letters of the secret of the holy Name are engraved above and below; at the time those letters flash and ascend toward other letters, all those holy camps travel in their journeys with awe and shame, since above there is none of those people of the world, they have no shame, they have no portion in the World to Come - to this point. Behold, it is explicit that the letters of the Name are engraved above and below, meaning in the supernal world and in the lower world, and therefore all the worlds are subjugated to do their Maker's will when they see the letters of the great Name before them - and therefore it follows from this that whoever has no shame of face has no portion in the World to Come, since he is not ashamed before the King before whom he has no portion in - for according to a person's soul's cleaving to the LORD, so he is bound in the supernal world - and one who is brazen of face distances himself from the LORD, since he is not afraid to sin before the King who is before him - and likewise, if they speak against him, he hardens his face to respond and is not ashamed before the supernal King, since there is no fear of God before his eyes - and therefore he has no portion in the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:94: And for the acquisition of this attribute, persistence is needed - that every day he free himself from his affairs for at least one hour, to think of the greatness of the Name and His wonders, and place fear of Him before him - and through this he shall be saved from sin, for whoever thinks of the LORD only occasionally does not have fear acquired in his heart, as Rabbeinu Yonah the Pious wrote in his commentary on Proverbs, and Rabbi Yosef Yavetz, peace be upon him, copied his words in his commentary on the chapters, on the mishnah "consider three things" (Avot, chapter 3, mishnah 1) - these are its words: the pious Rabbeinu Yonah wrote in the commentary on Proverbs (2:5), "then you shall understand the fear of the LORD, and find the knowledge of God" - two matters in the knowledge of the Name, blessed be He, and he gave a parable for them, saying: if you passed before the king once and did not remember his appearance, but if you see him again you shall remember that this is his appearance, for he is the king you saw - and another man passed before the king and remembered his appearance afterward, and it is found in his thought and his imaginative faculty has received it - is this one not more familiar with and knowing the king than the first? Therefore, whoever's soul has received knowledge of the loftiness of the Name, blessed be He, and His fear is upon his face without needing to prepare his heart and arrange his thought to bring it into his mind and picture it in his soul, is the one who [truly] knows the Name, blessed be He. And I say that since a person is, by his nature, inclined toward sins, he shall not be saved from the transgression that comes to hand unless he is crowned with the second level, which is the knowledge of God, for the scale of his nature tips toward guilt - but when the remembrance of the Name, blessed be He, is before his eyes always, the precious shall triumph over the vile - and behold, this supernal level is called, in this verse, "the knowledge of God," and therefore it is mentioned after fear, for it is the completion of fear - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:95: And when a person persists in thinking that the Shechinah is above, he shall come to purify his thoughts - and one can say this is what the Tanna intended in saying (Avot, chapter 2, mishnah 1), "know what is above you: a seeing eye, a hearing ear, and all your deeds are written in a book" - for these three things correspond to thought, speech, and deed, and therefore all three were necessary, and the last alone, which is inclusive - "and all your deeds are written in a book" - would not suffice. "A seeing eye" corresponds to imaginings, as it says (Jeremiah 20:12), "who sees the kidneys and the heart," and so King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 66:18), "if I had regarded iniquity in my heart" - and the intent is thought. "A hearing ear" corresponds to speech - if he spoke slander, or [if] his prayer, blessings, and Torah were said without fear, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 122a) - these are its words: and whoever's voice is heard there, whether in Torah, in prayer, or in crying out, without fear, immediately (Numbers 11:1), "and the LORD heard, and His anger burned, and the fire of the LORD burned among them" - to this point; and the reason, as explained there, is that hearing is judgment from the side of the left. "And all your deeds are written in a book" corresponds to deed, and it said "all," to include even deeds that involve neither mitzvah nor transgression, as Job, peace be upon him, said (Job 31:4), "does He not see my ways, and count all my steps?"
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:96: And in the Tikkunim (page 142b) it explained, concerning this mishnah, that the word "MaH" [what] above refers to the Shechinah standing over a person's head, who is called MaH, as is known. These are its words: and there are sins that are in secret, and the angels that go with the soul, of whom it is said (Psalms 91:11), "for He shall command His angels concerning you," cannot testify about them - behold, the Shechinah testifies about them - this is what is written (Jeremiah 23:24), "if a man hides in secret places," and so on - because the Shechinah is above his head, of whom it is said, "know what is above you: a seeing eye, a hearing ear, and all your deeds are written in a book" - to this point. And these designations mentioned - eye, ear, and book - are not distant from being found in her, as explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, end of page 256) - these are its words: she is called "eye" from the side of the right, "behold, the eye of the LORD is upon those who fear Him" (Psalms 33:18), and she is called "ear" from the side of the left, "incline Your ear, my God, and hear" (Daniel 9:18) - to this point. And for the designation "book," no proofs are needed, since it is agreed upon in Parashat Vayakhel (page 200a) and in the Tikkunim.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:97: And when a person persists in thinking that the Shechinah is above his head, and especially one who knows the matter of the Shechinah - and some of this matter has already been explained in the Gate of Fear - the acquisition of humility, with the conditions Ramban, peace be upon him, explained, shall not be distant from him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 7:1: After we have explained, in the previous chapters, the ways of humility, we must explain in this chapter how many attributes are found among the proud, all of which are hated before the Omnipresent, so that a person distance himself from them and be perfected in the attribute of humility properly.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 7:2: The first attribute by which the inclination deceives a person is that he arrange his clothing and style his hair and the like, and it appears that there is no transgression in this, and he does not know that from this he shall be drawn to the attribute of pride - for if they disgrace him, he shall say in his heart, do they disgrace a distinguished person like myself? And in Bereishit Rabbah (chapter 22:6) they, of blessed memory, said: Rabbi Ami said, the evil inclination does not walk to the sides, but in the middle of the plaza - and at the time it sees a person touching up his eyes, styling his hair, hanging [something ornamental] on his heel, it says, this one is mine - why? (Proverbs 26:12), "do you see a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him." Rabbi Avin said, whoever pampers his inclination in his youth, it shall eventually rebel against him in his old age - why? (Proverbs 29:21), "he who pampers his servant from youth, in the end he shall become a master" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 7:3: And so they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayeshev, page 190b) that the inclination's first grip on a person is in the arranging of his clothing - these are its words: (Genesis 39:12), "and she caught him by his garment, saying, lie with me" - "and she caught him by his garment" - for when the evil inclination rules over a person, he arranges and adorns his own clothing, styles his own hair - this is what is written, "and she caught him by his garment, saying, lie with me" - cling to me. Whoever is righteous strengthens himself against it and wages war against it - what is written? "And he left his garment in her hand and fled and went outside" - he abandons it and strengthens himself against it and flees from it, in order to be saved from it and that it not rule over him - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 7:4: Further, there (Zohar, Parashat Vayishlach, page 166a-b) - these are its words: Rabbi Shimon opened (Proverbs 12:9), "better one who is lowly and has a servant of his own, than one who honors himself and lacks bread" - this verse is said of the evil inclination, since it always accuses people - the evil inclination raises a person's heart and desire in pride, and he follows it, styling his hair and his head, until it becomes proud over him and draws him to Gehinnom. "But better one who is lowly" - this is one who does not follow the evil inclination and is not proud at all, but lowers his spirit, heart, and desire toward the Holy One, blessed be He - then that evil inclination is turned into "a servant of his own," unable to rule over him, and that person rules over it, along the lines of (Genesis 4:7), "and you shall rule over it." "One who honors himself" - as we have said, one who honors himself, styles his hair, becomes proud in his spirit - "and lacks bread" - lacks faith, along the lines of (Leviticus 21:22), "the bread of his God," and so on, "they offer the bread of their God" (ibid. 21:6) - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 7:5: Further, among the attributes of pride, it is copied in Sefer Beit Middot, at the end of the merit of proper conduct, and we shall copy all its words, since they also contain some of the attributes of humility - these are its words: fifteen things are said of a Torah scholar: pleasant in his house, pious in his sitting, shrewd in knowledge, sharp in his deeds, knows his own place, happy with his portion, does not take credit for himself, gives extensive answers, asks and answers, listens and answers on every point of a matter, goes to Torah scholars, and learns in order to practice.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 7:6: A Torah scholar must be modest in eating and drinking: he shall not eat standing, nor drink standing, nor wipe the plate clean, nor lick his fingers, nor belch in his fellow's presence - and he shall be modest in washing, in anointing, in his manner of dress, in his walking, in his voice, and in his good deeds.
